Each 5 ml contains 50 mg of Trimethoprim

items.t: Treatment of infections caused by trimethoprim-sensitive organisms, including urinary and respiratory tract infections.

src.q: Trimethoprim is indicated for the treatment of susceptible infections caused by trimethoprim - sensitive organisms including urinary tract and respiratory tract infections.

items.t: Prevention of recurrent urinary tract infections.

src.q: Trimethoprim is also indicated for the prevention of recurrent urinary tract infections.

items.t: Prevention and treatment of UTI, and treatment of other susceptible infections, in adults and children.

src.q: Trimethoprim is indicated for the prevention and treatment of urinary tract infections in adults and children

restrictions.note: No specialist-only, shared-care or brand restrictions found in the tablet SmPC, the suspension SmPC, SPS or MHRA pages checked. Dialysis use is specialist-supervised (see renal).

items.t: Adults and children over 12 years: 200 mg TWICE DAILY. Duration 3 days (e.g. uncomplicated cystitis in women) up to 2 weeks, by type and severity of infection. The first dose can be doubled.

src.q: Adults and children over 12 years of age: 200 mg twice daily

Treatment should continue for a period of between 3 days (e.g. uncomplicated bacterial cystitis in women) to 2 weeks depending on the nature and severity of the infection. The first dose can be doubled.

items.t: Adults and children over 12 years: 100 mg ONCE daily AT NIGHT.

src.q: Long-term treatment and prophylactic therapy: Adults and children over 12 years: 100 mg at night

items.t: Adults and children over 12 years: 200 mg (20 ml) TWICE DAILY.

src.q: Treatment of urinary tract infections and all other susceptible infections: 200 mg (20 ml) twice daily.

items.t: Adults and children over 12 years: 100 mg (10 ml) at night.

src.q: Long-term prevention of recurrent urinary tract infections: 100 mg (10 ml) at night.

items.t: Elderly: dose depends on kidney function (see renal).

src.q: Elderly Depending on kidney function, see special dosage schedule.

items.t: Tablets, children 6 to 12 years: 100 mg twice daily for acute infections; 50 mg at night for long-term/prophylaxis.

src.q: Children 6 years to 12 years: 100 mg twice daily
Children 6 years to 12 years of age: 50 mg at night.

items.t: Tablets are not suitable under 6 years; use a suspension. The same SmPC's prophylaxis section also says the tablet is not suitable under 12 years (internal inconsistency in the source).

src.q: This dosage form is not suitable for use in children younger than 6 years; a more suitable dosage form (such as a suspension) should be used in this age group.
This dosage form is not suitable for use in children younger than 12 years; a more suitable dosage form (such as a suspension) should be used in this age group.

items.t: Suspension, children 6 weeks to 12 years, UTI treatment: 8 mg/kg daily in two equal doses. Suggested: 6 weeks-5 months 25 mg (2.5 ml) twice daily; 6 months-5 years 50 mg (5 ml) twice daily; 6-12 years 100 mg (10 ml) twice daily.

src.q: Children 6 weeks to 12 years of age Treatment of urinary tract infections is based on a dosage of 8 mg/kg body weight daily, subdivided into two equal doses.
25 mg (2.5 ml) twice daily 50 mg (5 ml) twice daily 100 mg (10 ml) twice daily

items.t: Suspension, long-term prevention of recurrent UTI: 2 mg/kg daily as a single dose at night. Suggested: 6 months-5 years 25 mg (2.5 ml); 6-12 years 50 mg (5 ml) at night.

src.q: Long-term prevention of recurrent urinary tract infection is based on 2 mg/kg body weight daily given as a single dose at night.
25 mg (2.5 ml) at night 50 mg (5 ml) at night

items.t: Lower age limit differs by SmPC: tablet SmPC says do not give to premature infants or children under 4 months; suspension SmPC says do not give to premature infants and neonates under 6 weeks.

src.q: Trimethoprim should not be administered to pregnant women, premature infants or children under 4 months of age
premature infants and neonates under 6 weeks

items.t: Take particular care with blood monitoring in children on long-term therapy.

src.q: Particular care should be exercised in the haematological monitoring of children on long term therapy.

items.t: Hypersensitivity to trimethoprim or any excipient.

src.q: Hypersensitivity to the active substance or to any of the excipients listed in section 6.1.

items.t: Severe hepatic insufficiency.

src.q: Trimethoprim is contra-indicated in severe hepatic insufficiency.

items.t: Megaloblastic anaemia and other blood dyscrasias.

src.q: Trimethoprim is contra-indicated in megaloblastic anaemia and other blood dyscrasias.

items.t: First trimester of pregnancy (the tablet SmPC 4.3 also says it should not be given to pregnant women, without naming a trimester).

src.q: Trimethoprim is contra-indicated in first trimester of pregnancy
Trimethoprim should not be administered to pregnant women, premature infants or children under 4 months of age

items.t: Premature infants and young infants - SmPCs differ: tablet SmPC 4.3 says under 4 months; suspension SmPC 4.3 says neonates under 6 weeks.

src.q: Trimethoprim should not be administered to pregnant women, premature infants or children under 4 months of age
Trimethoprim should not be administered to pregnant women (first trimester of pregnancy (see section 4.6)), premature infants and neonates under 6 weeks.

items.t: Hyperkalaemia: closely monitor electrolytes in patients at risk (renal insufficiency, poorly controlled diabetes, potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements or salt substitutes, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, heparin).

src.q: Close monitoring of serum electrolytes is advised in patients at risk for hyperkalaemia (see section 4.8).
Patients at risk for the development of hyperkalaemia include those with renal insufficiency, poorly controlled diabetes mellitus

items.t: Folate deficiency (actual or potential, e.g. elderly): use with caution; consider a folate supplement. Trimethoprim may depress haemopoiesis.

src.q: Caution should be exercised in the administration of trimethoprim to patients with actual or potential folate deficiency (e.g. the elderly). Administration of a folate supplement should be considered.
Trimethoprim may cause depression of haemopoiesis.

items.t: Marked renal impairment: avoid accumulation and haematological toxicity; dialysis patients only under specialist (infection + renal) supervision.

src.q: In patients with marked impairment of renal function, care should be taken to avoid accumulation and resulting adverse haematological effects.
Trimethoprim should only be initiated and used in dialysis patients under close supervision from specialists in both infectious disease and renal medicine.

items.t: Severe cutaneous reactions (SJS, TEN, DRESS): stop immediately if signs appear; never restart after SJS/TEN/DRESS.

src.q: If signs and symptoms suggestive of these reactions appear, trimethoprim should be withdrawn immediately
If the patient has developed a serious reaction such as SJS, TEN or DRESS with the use of trimethoprim, the treatment must not be restarted in this patient at any time.

items.t: Acute porphyria: tablet SmPC says use with caution; suspension SmPC says avoid if known or suspected risk.

src.q: Caution should be used in patients with acute porphyria.
If a patient has a known or suspected risk of acute prophyria, treatment with trimethoprim should be avoided.

items.t: Neonates: use only under careful medical supervision (tablet SmPC).

src.q: Trimethoprim should be used under careful medical supervision in neonates.

items.t: Tablets contain lactose; suspension: patients with hereditary fructose intolerance should not take it.

src.q: Each tablet contains 50 mg lactose
Patients with rare hereditary problems of fructose intolerance should not take this medicine.

items.t: Methotrexate: tablet SmPC says avoid (increased antifolate effect); suspension SmPC says risk of haematological toxicity. SPS: avoid; if unavoidable, frequent FBC.

src.q: Trimethoprim increases the antifolate effect of methotrexate therefore use should be avoided.
Avoid prescribing co-trimoxazole or trimethoprim with methotrexate, due to the risk of severe bone marrow suppression.

items.t: Potassium-raising medicines (potassium-sparing diuretics, potassium supplements, ACE inhibitors/ARBs, heparin): risk of significant hyperkalaemia; monitor potassium.

src.q: Concomitant use of drugs that may increase serum potassium levels may lead to a significant increase in serum potassium.
Monitoring of potassium should be undertaken as appropriate (see section 4.4).

items.t: Warfarin and other coumarins: trimethoprim may increase the anticoagulant effect.

src.q: Trimethoprim may potentiate the anticoagulant effect of warfarin and other coumarins.

items.t: Dapsone: plasma levels of both drugs may rise.

src.q: Dapsone: Plasma concentrations of trimethoprim and dapsone may increase when taken together.

items.t: Other folate antagonists: may cause folate deficiency in predisposed patients.

src.q: Trimethoprim may induce folate deficiency in patients predisposed to folate deficiency such as those receiving concomitant folate antagonists or anticonvulsants.

items.t: Diuretics (mainly thiazides) in elderly: more thrombocytopenia with purpura.

src.q: In elderly patients concurrently taking diuretics, primarily thiazides, there is an increased incidence of thrombocytopenia with purpura.

items.t: Digoxin, phenytoin (careful monitoring), procainamide, ciclosporin (nephrotoxicity), repaglinide (hypoglycaemia; monitor glucose), rifampicin, pyrimethamine.

src.q: Careful monitoring of patients treated with digoxin or phenytoin is advised
Monitoring of blood glucose is advised if co-administered with repaglinide (see section 4.5).

items.t: eGFR over 30: normal dose. eGFR 15 to 30: normal dose for 3 days, then half dose. eGFR under 15: half the normal dose. Measure: both the tablet and suspension SmPCs name the measure eGFR, but print the unit as "ml/min" (not ml/min/1.73 m2); the thresholds are kept as eGFR because that is the measure the sources name. If only CrCl is known, treat the bands as approximate.

src.q: Dosage advised where there is reduced kidney function: eGFR (ml/min) Dosage advised Over 30 Normal 15- 30 Normal for 3 days then half dose Under 15 Half the normal dose
Dosage advised eGFR (ml/min)

items.t: Consider monitoring renal function and electrolytes, especially with longer use. Dialysis: start and use only under close specialist supervision (infection + renal); trimethoprim is removed by dialysis.

src.q: Monitoring of renal function and serum electrolytes should be considered particularly with longer term use, in patients with impaired renal function.
Trimethoprim is removed by dialysis.

items.t: Contraindicated in severe hepatic insufficiency. Fatal haematological effects have been reported especially in elderly or those with renal or hepatic impairment.

src.q: Trimethoprim is contra-indicated in severe hepatic insufficiency.
Fatalities have been reported (especially in the elderly, or those with impairment of renal or hepatic function in whom careful monitoring is advised

items.t: First trimester: contraindicated (increased risk of miscarriage and malformations, including neural tube defects, oral clefts and heart defects; folate interference).

src.q: Trimethoprim is contraindicated during the first trimester of pregnancy (see section 4.3).
in particular neural tube defects, oral clefts and cardiovascular defects

items.t: Second and third trimesters: avoid unless clinically necessary. Note: both SmPCs also contain a broader line in 4.6 ("contra-indicated in pregnant women"), and the tablet SmPC 4.3 says it should not be given to pregnant women without naming a trimester; the trimester-specific advice is shown here.

src.q: In the second and third trimesters, use should be avoided, unless clinically necessary.
Trimethoprim is contra-indicated in pregnant women, premature infants or infants during the first few weeks of life.
Trimethoprim should not be administered to pregnant women, premature infants or children under 4 months of age

items.t: BUMPS (UKTIS patient leaflet): usually avoided in early pregnancy because it can lower folate; if needed in early pregnancy it is usually given with high-dose folic acid. Other antibiotics are usually used first for UTI.

src.q: Trimethoprim is usually avoided in early pregnancy because it can lower folate levels in your body.
If trimethoprim is needed in early pregnancy, it is usually prescribed with a high-dose folic acid supplement to help maintain folate levels.

items.t: Tablet SmPC: excreted in breast milk but not contraindicated for short-term use.

src.q: Trimethoprim is excreted in breast milk but is not contra-indicated for short term use in lactating mothers.

items.t: Suspension SmPC: effects on the suckling child are likely; contraindicated if the breastfed infant is under 4 months. (The two SmPCs differ; both statements concern trimethoprim in milk, so both are shown whatever the formulation.)

src.q: Effects on the suckling child are likely if therapeutic doses are administered to breast-feeding mothers.
Trimethoprim is contraindicated if the breast fed infant is less than 4 months of age.

items.t: Usual caution when prescribing for women of child-bearing age.

src.q: The usual caution in prescribing any drug for women of child bearing age should be exercised with trimethoprim.

items.t: BUMPS: no evidence that use by the father around conception affects the baby.

src.q: There is no evidence that trimethoprim taken by the father before or around the time of conception affects the baby.

items.t: Very common: hyperkalaemia. Common: headache, nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting, rash, urticaria, candida (monilial) overgrowth.

src.q: Very common: Hyperkalaemia
Common: Nausea, diarrhoea, vomiting.
Common: Skin rashes, urticaria
Common: Monilial overgrowth

items.t: Blood disorders (very rare: neutropenia, agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia, pancytopenia; megaloblastic anaemia; methaemoglobinaemia). Tell patients to seek immediate help for fever, sore throat, rash, mouth ulcers, purpura, bruising or bleeding.

src.q: Very rare: Leucopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, pancytopaenia, bone marrow depression, agranulocytosis, aplastic anaemia
advised to seek immediate medical attention if symptoms such as fever, sore throat, rash, mouth ulcers, purpura, bruising or bleeding develop.

items.t: SJS, TEN, DRESS: stop at once; never restart.

src.q: the treatment must not be restarted in this patient at any time.

items.t: Cholestatic jaundice and hepatic necrosis (very rare, may be fatal); aseptic meningitis (recurs on re-exposure); anaphylaxis, angioedema.

src.q: Cholestatic jaundice and hepatic necrosis may be fatal.
Very rare: Hypersensitivity, anaphylaxis, angioedema

items.t: Long-term treatment or folate-deficiency risk (e.g. elderly): regular blood counts for pancytopenia.

src.q: Regular haematological tests should be undertaken in patients receiving long term treatment and those predisposed to folate deficiency, (e.g. the elderly), to check for possible pancytopaenia.

items.t: Serum potassium if at risk of hyperkalaemia or taking potassium-raising medicines.

src.q: If concomitant use of the above-mentioned agents is deemed appropriate, monitoring of serum potassium is recommended (see section 4.5).

items.t: Folic acid deficiency: give calcium folinate, check response; stopping trimethoprim may be needed.

src.q: If there is evidence of folic acid deficiency, calcium folinate should be administered and response checked by haematologic monitoring. It may be necessary to discontinue trimethoprim.

items.t: Oral. Where a single daily dose is used, taking it at bedtime may maximise urinary concentrations.

src.q: Where a single dose is required, dosage at bedtime may maximise urinary concentrations.

items.t: Tablet breakline is for ease of swallowing only, not for dividing into equal doses.

src.q: The breakline is only to facilitate breaking for ease of swallowing and not to divide into equal doses.

items.t: Seek immediate medical help for fever, sore throat, rash, mouth ulcers, purpura, bruising or bleeding.

src.q: Patients and their carers should be told how to recognise signs of blood disorders

src.q: Patients should be advised of the signs and symptoms and monitored closely for skin reactions.
